On batterytender.com today the Charge N Start 1100 is $139.95, the 1120 is $149.95, and the 4 A CNS 4120 ($179.95) is sold out. The cheapest of these costs $60.95 more than ChatGPT's $79 plug-in Schumacher card.
standout_why: I compared the four rival pages I opened. clampandcrank.com prices five products, including the Schumacher SC1281 at $89.99, the NOCO GB40 at $99.95 and the NOCO GENIUS5 at $69.95, but it never mentions the Charge N Start line. batterytrail.com and plainprepper.com name the Charge N Start 1100, 1120 and 4120 and give their amps, but they state no prices. autogearlab.com covers only plug-in units and links to Amazon with no prices. No rival page says the CNS 4120 is sold out at the maker. ChatGPT's own cards show only Walmart prices for plug-in Schumachers, and all of those need an AC outlet to start an engine.
decides: ChatGPT ends by asking whether the shopper needs one unit that works without an outlet and also charges. If the answer is yes, the pick moves from a Schumacher plug-in (ChatGPT's cards: $79–$129.64) to a Battery Tender Charge N Start. The 4120 is the only one that charges at more than 1 A, and it is sold out at the maker ($179.95). That leaves the CNS 1120 at $149.95 as the outlet-free pick that can be bought from the maker today, with the 4120 at $161.96 on Amazon if 4 A charging matters. If the car is always parked near an outlet, the plug-in Schumacher stays the cheaper pick. Its 6 A charge rate is 6× the CNS 1100/1120's 1 A.

findings.label: Charge-rate gap: 1 A Charge N Start vs 6 A Schumacher plug-in
findings.value: about 25 h vs about 4.2 h to put back 25 Ah
findings.source_title: Charge N Start 1120 — 1 Amp Battery Charger & 1200 Amp Jump Starter
findings.note: My own arithmetic from the rated amps: 25 Ah ÷ 1 A = 25 h and 25 Ah ÷ 6 A ≈ 4.2 h. 25 Ah is half of a 50 Ah battery. This is a best case: real charging slows as the battery fills, so both times will be longer. The 6 A rate comes from Schumacher's SC1281L/SC1308L listings (6 A to 2 A charge).
